title: Polynomial-Time Computability of the Middle Word
statement: The function that first deletes the first four bits of a Boolean word and then applies the specified one-pass transducer is computable by a finite Turing machine in polynomial time: there exist natural numbers $C$ and $c$ such that, on every input word of length $n$, the machine halts within $C(n+1)^c$ steps and outputs the resulting word.
